claim_verdicts.source: Chrome 153.0.8010.53 headless via CDP (Tracing devtools.timeline), reviewer scratch run on git show stage-0:www/*.html served from 127.0.0.1:8099; no HTML/MDN/Chrome docs root in versions.yaml, none under refs/
claim_verdicts.evidence: Every frame traced after a change ran the steps in this order: UpdateLayoutTree (style recalculation: which CSS applies to which element), then Layout (when needed), then PrePaint/Paint, then raster/draw. Font-size edit on h1: UpdateLayoutTree 1 -> Layout 1 (5 of 23 layout objects dirty) -> Paint. The lesson's 'a few steps' list omits compositing/raster, which is fine at this level; the order stated is what the trace shows.

issues.quote: Switching to another tab and back
issues.text: q5 option d is keyed wrong ('Switching tabs leaves the page's DOM and CSS as they were'), but returning to a tab can make the browser render the page again. Chrome 153 headless, index.html, trace across hide/show (visibilityState visible -> hidden -> visible): one run 0 Layout/Paint, another run (other tab about:blank) UpdateLayoutTree 2, Layout 3, Paint 2. The lesson's own rule ('renders again whenever a change affects what is visible') also lets a learner argue the page became visible again. Ambiguous key.
issues.fix: Replace q5 option d (en) with "Saving a new heading into index.html on the server, without reloading the page" (vi: "Lưu heading mới vào index.html trên server mà không tải lại trang"). Explanation d (en): "The browser renders the DOM it already has; it does not see the changed file until the page is loaded again." (vi to match). In explanation.correct, replace "and switching tabs does not change its DOM or CSS" with "and a changed file on the server does not reach the page until it is reloaded".

issues.quote: The Styles pane beside the tree lists its CSS; click inside the empty `element.style { }` block at the top
issues.text: Unlisted claim: a specific DevTools UI fact (an element.style block at the top of the Styles pane, editable by clicking) is not in the ledger. It is true: the DevTools bundle served by Chrome 153 (panels/elements/elements.js) labels the inline-style section "element.style" (`...:"element.style"`), and CDP CSS.getInlineStylesForNode on the h1 with no style attribute returned an editable inline style (r1 CSS.setStyleTexts edit succeeded). Only the ledger entry is missing.
issues.fix: Add to frontend.l1.render.meta.json a claim 9: {"text": "In Chrome/Edge DevTools, the Styles pane of the Elements panel shows an element.style block at the top for the selected element, where inline declarations can be typed.", "kind": "behavior", "section": 7, "needs_verification": true, "source_hint": "DevTools bundle panels/elements (element.style section)"}. No lesson text change.

issues.quote: Flutter, which the Đơn Hàng app is built with, faces the same trade-off, as the next module shows.
issues.text: 'Flutter' is not in known_vocab and is not defined here. I also did not know Đơn Hàng has an app separate from the backend, so this sentence tells me nothing I can use. The same name returns in summary line 5 as 'Flutter's pipeline'.
issues.fix: Delete this sentence from §4 and keep the Flutter pointer only in Connections, where it already is (and drop the Flutter half of summary line 5, see next issue).

issues.quote: 5. A page that changes its DOM constantly renders constantly, the same concern Flutter's pipeline has.
issues.text: The lesson never mentions a Flutter 'pipeline'; the only pipeline I know is the ASP.NET middleware one. The first half of the line is established, the second half is new.
issues.fix: End summary line 5 without 'the same concern Flutter's pipeline has', e.g. '...renders constantly, and every render costs work.'

issues.quote: Changing the colour of a heading changes no sizes or positions, so the browser can skip layout and only paint the heading again.
issues.text: The diagram's first step is 'match CSS to elements'. For a colour change the text says layout is skipped and paint runs, but not whether the matching step runs again. I could not tell whether a CSS change always re-runs that first step.
issues.fix: Add half a sentence saying what happens to the first step, e.g. 'it re-matches the heading's styles, skips layout, and only paints the heading again'.

issues.quote: Now imagine a page that changes its DOM sixty times a second, or one that changes a single colour. Does the browser do the same amount of work for both
issues.text: The two pages differ in two ways at once (how often, and what kind of change). The lesson mostly answers 'what kind' (colour vs size), so the comparison I was primed for is only half answered.
issues.fix: Make the contrast match the answer: 'a page that changes a heading's colour, and one that changes its size', or keep 'sixty times a second' and contrast it with 'once'.

issues.quote: Open the Rendering panel (menu ⋮ → More tools → Rendering)
issues.text: The browser window and the developer tools each have a ⋮ menu with 'More tools'. I would likely click the browser's one first and not find Rendering there.
issues.fix: Write 'the developer tools' own ⋮ menu (top right of the tools panel) → More tools → Rendering'.

issues.quote: In the Styles pane, add `color: red` to its style
issues.text: The DOM lesson taught me the Elements tab, but not the Styles pane or how to add a property there. I would have to guess where to click and type.
issues.fix: Add one clause: 'in the Styles pane beside the element tree, click inside the empty element.style { } block at the top and type `color: red`'.

issues.quote: "Changing CSS is free and never triggers any of the same rendering work a DOM change does."
issues.text: I had to re-read this belief twice; 'never triggers any of the same rendering work a DOM change does' is a mouthful and does not sound like something I would think in those words.
issues.fix: Shorten to: "Changing CSS is cheap; only DOM changes make the browser do real work."

issues.quote: False, because any visible change to the DOM or CSS makes the browser render again.
issues.text: q2: the correct option nearly restates the Core concepts definition ('it happens again whenever a change affects what is visible'), so I can match wording instead of understanding.
issues.fix: Rephrase option c around concrete cases, e.g. 'False, because editing text or resizing the window makes the browser render again.'

issues.quote: Changing its colour back to black
issues.text: q3: options b and c are the same idea (a colour change) and d changes nothing, so once I rule out colour only a is left, without reasoning about layout.
issues.fix: Replace c with a tempting alternative, e.g. 'Changing its background colour to yellow' or 'Changing its text to another word of the same length'.

issues.quote: A wider box moves the products around it, forcing layout and more paint; a colour only needs a repaint.
issues.text: q4: the correct option is by far the longest and the only one that mentions both versions, so it can be picked by length alone.
issues.fix: Give one or two distractors the same two-part shape, e.g. 'Both only change CSS, so both cost one repaint; the stutter comes from the list being long.'

issues.quote: The file on the server staying the same
issues.text: q5: option c is not an event at all, so nobody would pick it. Option d relies on 'page source' / 'View source', which the lesson never mentions, and I was unsure whether leaving the tab and coming back counts as a visible change.
issues.fix: Replace c with a tempting non-trigger such as 'Selecting the heading in the Elements tab', and reword d as 'Reading the heading's text in the Elements tab without editing it'.
